method: All pages in the cited phases 2–5 manifest were inspected in consecutive image sequences, plus four sparse full-context sheets and eight full 1600x900 source frames. Contact sheets are cropped and uniformly reduced; no interpolation or synthesis. This is not a claim that every source frame was inspected or audio was auditioned.
observations: Both arm sequences show a detached articulated part, continued approach/use of the available arm, then collapse without the missing arm returning. One body retains a seated/kneeling result; the other folds farther forward/sideways.
The head visibly separates into an independent part. The second subject collapses after the leg-loss event; overlapping geometry limits direct inspection of the detached leg and its floor contacts.

The six deaths develop different orientations and bent limb configurations, with contact between the upper group and between the lower bodies. No gross explosive separation, mesh stretching or bind-pose reset was observed within these windows.

Phase 5 +5.0–6.25 seconds shows a largely stable pile at the reviewed scale. The upper cluster remains in supported-looking bent/kneeling poses; this is not an approval of all contact aesthetics or proof of zero movement.
limits: Body/weapon overlap hides some stump and support contacts. Technical regional/physics checks supply separate evidence, not visual proof of hidden surfaces.

Small remaining adjustments and supported kneeling shapes remain artistically provisional. The opt-in corpse_motion.csv telemetry was not recorded in this capture; no maximum late velocity is inferred.
Phase 5 end checks report 32 awake bodies out of a 96 peak and 3 frozen corpses, not that every body sleeps.
Fresh-hit resume and later settling have a separate bounded review; this manifest only covers its listed intervals.
Review concerns scripted physicality through the actual gameplay camera; ordinary-input packaged evidence is separate.
